all.title: V-BOUNDS makes conformance to the locked λ tuning range a failing sabotage, and the range is never routed to Round 4
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:117 (§1 row 10), :233 (G2-6), :488 (V-BOUNDS), :633 (mile-0 'Half-life call' row), :610 (locks table)
all.claim: ARCHITECTURE.md §4 is LOCKED. It fixes λ as runtime-configurable with a tuning range of 1 minute to 24 hours. The paper treats that range as a v1 code detail (`decay.py:34-35`) and 'decouples' the recall half-life from it as a local design call. V-BOUNDS then lists 'v1's DecayConfig bounds used for the recall λ' as the sabotage the check must catch, so an implementation that honors the locked range fails a v7 check. The mile-0 row for the half-life call cites ARCHITECTURE.md:82 only as '(λ runtime-configurable; silent on history)' and leaves out the range on that same line. The locks table row for decay (:610) says 'Kept'. Counterexample: v6's own example, `recallHalfLife: 1209600.0` (14 days, BLUEPRINT_v6.md:263), is outside the locked 24 h ceiling. Under v7 it becomes legal constitution content, applied as an exponential decay at read time, with no §9 brief naming the clause it overrides.
all.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:82 ('Tuning range: 1 minute to 24 hours'), :6 and :349 (changes need §9); CLAUDE.md:35 (lock 2: decay math); src/moneta/decay.py:33-35 (comment 'Tuning range per MONETA.md §2.3'); BLUEPRINT_v7.md:117, :233, :488, :633
all.proposed_fix: Add a Round 4 item, 'E5: recall half-life outside ARCHITECTURE.md:82's 1 min–24 h range'. Cite :82 in full in the mile-0 table. Until that item is ruled, either make the locked range X1's ceiling for the recall λ (so V-BOUNDS checks against :82) or drop the V-BOUNDS sabotage. Change the locks-table decay row from 'Kept' to 'Kept, except the tuning range: Round 4'.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds against the sources. ARCHITECTURE.md:82 says, inside a document marked LOCKED (:3, :6, :349): "λ is runtime-configurable. ... Tuning range: 1 minute to 24 hours." MONETA.md:88 (§2.3) repeats it, and src/moneta/decay.py:33-35 implements it with the comment "Tuning range per MONETA.md §2.3".

The paper never cites :82's range as a locked clause. Every mention treats the bounds as v1 code:
- BLUEPRINT_v7.md:117 (§1 row 10): "v1 bounds are 60 s to 24 h (decay.py:34-35)".
- :233 (G2-6): bounds are "decoupled from v1's DecayConfig range".
- :590 (Q9): "hard-coded 60 s – 24 h (decay.py:34-35)".
- :706: the same.

The mile-0 row (:633) cites ARCHITECTURE.md:82 only as "(λ runtime-configurable; silent on history)" and leaves out the range on that same line.

V-BOUNDS (:488) lists "v1's DecayConfig bounds used for the recall λ" as a sabotage. An implementation that honors the locked range would therefore fail a v7 check. Row 10 also makes v6's 14-day example (BLUEPRINT_v6.md:263) legal even though it exceeds the locked 24 h.

The locks table (:610) says "Kept" for decay and routes only the evaluation-point question to Round 4 (O2). Nothing routes the range. RULINGS.md and pass1_rulings_brief.md:138 also call the bounds v1's (decay.py:34-35) and never rule on the range. So no owner ruling covers this, and raising it does not reopen anything ruled.

The best rebuttal is that the recall λ is a different quantity from the locked retention λ, so :82 doesn't bind it. The paper can't make that argument by assertion. At :233-234 and :610 it already concedes that whether the lock reaches the recall fold (O2) is a Round 4 question, not a local call. The range is the same question, and it is the one left unrouted.

Severity "critical" is arguably high for a design paper, but the defect is real and needs the owner.
verdicts.better_fix:
The direction is right, with three refinements:

1. **Route it as part of O2, or pair it with O2, rather than as a free-standing "E5".** The underlying question is the same: does ARCHITECTURE.md §4's λ, with its range at :82, bind the recall λ? Put it this way: "O2b: do :82's runtime-configurable λ and its 1 min–24 h tuning range govern λ_recall?" If it stays separate, label it a question, not an E-item, since E1–E4 are v5's exceptions.

2. **Don't drop the V-BOUNDS sabotage. Recast it.** The real defect Q9 targets is bounds hard-coded in code instead of read from the journal. Make the sabotage "the recall bounds hard-coded rather than read from the constitution". Until Round 4 rules, set X1's recall-λ ceiling to :82's range, so a conforming implementation passes. Also keep the 14-day example in row 10 out-of-range until the ruling, instead of using it as justification.

3. **Fix every citation, not only mile-0.**
   - Cite ARCHITECTURE.md:82 and MONETA.md:88 as the source of the range at :117, :233, :590 and :706, and keep decay.py:34-35 only as the implementation.
   - At :633, cite :82 in full.
   - At :610, change "Kept" to "Kept for retention; whether :82's range binds the recall λ goes to Round 4."

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds up against the sources. ARCHITECTURE.md:82 is a locked clause: "λ is runtime-configurable. Starting value: half-life of 6 hours. Tuning range: 1 minute to 24 hours." The doc header (ARCHITECTURE.md:3,6) and footer say changes need a MONETA.md §9 escalation. v1's bounds are the code form of that clause: src/moneta/decay.py:33-35 carries the comment "Tuning range per MONETA.md §2.3 ('1 minute to 24 hours')", and set_half_life raises an error outside that range (decay.py:91-97).

The paper only ever presents the range as a v1 code detail:
- BLUEPRINT_v7.md:117 says "v1 bounds are 60 s to 24 h (src/moneta/decay.py:34-35)".
- :233 says "decoupled from v1's DecayConfig range (decay.py:34-35,92)".
- :590 (Q9) says "hard-coded 60 s – 24 h (decay.py:34-35)".
- :706 lists ":34-35 bounds of 60 s – 24 h".

None of these cite ARCHITECTURE.md:82's range. :633 and :761 cite :82 only as "λ runtime-configurable". The open-questions table has O2 at :667, but O2 asks only whether the recall fold is a fourth evaluation point under :90. No Round 4 item names the tuning range, and the locks row at :610 says "Kept". V-BOUNDS at :488 does list "v1's DecayConfig bounds used for the recall λ" as the sabotage. So an implementation that applies the locked range to the recall λ would be marked as sabotage, and v6's 14-day example (BLUEPRINT_v6.md:263, quoted at :117) would become legal with no §9 brief.

The strongest rebuttal: the paper's position (G2-8, :235) is that the recall fold is a separate pure view, not the retention λ of §4, so the locked range arguably applies only to the retention λ. But the paper never makes that argument for the range. It routes only the evaluation-point question (O2) to Round 4, not the range. Whether §4's range binds a second exponential decay applied at read time is exactly the kind of spec question the paper itself says is "not a local call" (:235). So the gap is real.

On severity: "critical" is somewhat high. The paper does flag the 14-day conflict, but against the wrong authority (code, not the lock). The fix needs owner and Round 4 routing, not a redesign.
verdicts.better_fix:
The fix is mostly right; I'd adjust four things.

(1) Route the range question as an open question that sits beside O2, not as a separate E-item. Better still, widen O2 to ask "is the recall fold governed by ARCHITECTURE.md §4 (:82 range and :90 evaluation points)?" Both questions have the same premise: whether the fold is a separate pure view. If it gets its own item, call it O-something, with the default "the fold is a view, so the recall λ is not bound by :82" [P] and the fallback "the recall bounds are capped at 1 min–24 h". That fallback also means v6's 14-day example must be replaced.

(2) Re-cite the range everywhere as ARCHITECTURE.md:82 (lock), with decay.py:33-35 as its implementation: rows :117, :233, :590 and :706, plus the :633 and :761 cite text.

(3) In the V-BOUNDS row (:488), make the sabotage conditional until Round 4 rules. Pending the ruling, either drop it or reword it to "bounds hard-coded outside the journal" (that is the actual Q9 failure, :590), not "the locked range applied".

(4) Change the locks row at :610 to "Kept, except whether :82's tuning range binds the recall λ: Round 4". Flag for the owner that R2 (recall_half_life) stays as ruled. Only its legal range is open.

all.title: An agent read needs a context and scopes, but the locked query(embedding, limit) carries neither, and the paper still claims signatures are unchanged
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:80 ('No fifth op… signatures don't change'), :204 (Resolved(c, n)), :434 (P1), :463 (X3), :609 (locks table)
all.claim: P1 and G2-1 say a read depends on (journal prefix, embedding, limit, context, scopes, t), and G2 resolves policy per context `c`. The locked agent read is `query(embedding: List[float], limit: int = 5)`, which takes no context, no scopes and no time. v6 says v5's read is `recall(embedding, limit, context, scopes, time)`. That is a different signature. The paper never says how an agent's read reaches a context and scopes. Each possible answer breaks something the paper locks or claims. (1) Add parameters to `query`: that breaks lock 1 and X3. (2) Expose v5's `recall` to agents: that is a fifth agent op. (3) Read context and scopes from harness or process state: then the read depends on state that is not in G1 (QueryRecords are host-owned, :247), which breaks G2-1 'reads no file, no clock'. O14 sends the analogous signal_attention echo to §9 (:679), but this read-side gap gets no O-item and no Round 4 row.
all.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:37 (query signature), :33 (no fifth op without §9); src/moneta/api.py:378-380, :399 (time.time()); BLUEPRINT_v6.md:95 (v5 recall takes context and scopes); BLUEPRINT_v7.md:204, :228, :434, :463
all.proposed_fix: State the binding explicitly. One option: context and scopes are fixed per store or session by a journaled harness op, and `query` resolves against the context journaled live at that seq. That keeps the signature and G2-1. Otherwise, add a Round 4 row for a `query` signature change or a context-bearing read, and add a check (V-QUERYSIG) that asserts the four signatures are byte-identical to ARCHITECTURE.md §2.

verdicts.reason: The core gap is real; I could not refute it. The locked read is `query(embedding, limit)` (ARCHITECTURE.md:37; src/moneta/api.py:379). It takes no context, scopes or time, and it reads `time.time()` at api.py:399. BLUEPRINT_v7.md:80 and X3 (:463) say the four signatures don't change. Yet P1 (:434) says a read depends on (prefix, embedding, limit, context, scopes, t), and G2 resolves `Resolved(c, n)` per context (:204, :224-225). v6:95 confirms that v5's `recall` takes context and scopes, and that scopes change slot outcomes. I searched v7 for session, binding, caller and context-selection language and found nothing that says how a `query()` call picks `c` or the caller's scopes. The only mentions are QueryRecord fields (:248-249), which the host fills in after the fact, and open question 4 at :689. P1's status column marks the claim false in v1 only because of the clock and the in-place write (api.py:399-401). It says nothing about the missing context and scope inputs. RULINGS.md has no ruling on context or scope binding, so this doesn't reopen a ruled item. The finding overreaches in one place. Its option (3), taking context and scopes from harness or process state, does not by itself break G2-1. G2-1 (:228) is purity of `Resolved(c, n)` given `c`; how `c` gets chosen is outside it. And G3's host-owned QueryRecord already logs context and scopes (:248-249), so replay can survive if the host records the binding. What option (3) breaks is the paper's silence: the binding source is then unjournaled host state that the paper never names, and no check covers it. The finding also correctly notes that the write-side analogue has O14 and §9 handling (:341-343, :679) while the read side gets no O-item and no Round 4 row. Severity "major" is fair, because G2's per-context resolution and slot/scope semantics can't reach an agent read as currently specified.
verdicts.better_fix: The direction is right, but the fix should list the cheapest option first and say more about the journaled-binding option. (a) Cheapest option: v7.0 has exactly one root context and the full scope set, and v1 has no multi-caller authorization. Then context and scopes are constants, P1 reduces to (prefix, embedding, limit, t), and per-context binding becomes an explicit v7.x item. (b) If a binding op is used, add it to the G1 event-kind table (:134-150) with its signed-set status, and say whether the binding is per store, per session or per caller. Scopes are caller authorization, so a store-wide binding quietly merges callers; state that. (c) Either way, have `query` read the binding as journaled at the live seq. That keeps G2-1 and lets the host QueryRecord (:248-249) carry the bound context and scopes for replay. (d) Add an O-item next to O14 with a Round 4 / §9 row for a context-bearing read if per-caller scopes are wanted later. (e) Add V-QUERYSIG, asserting the four signatures match ARCHITECTURE.md §2 byte for byte, plus a sabotage case: a read that resolves against an unjournaled or draft context.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this finding. The paper does not handle the gap. The locked read is `query(embedding: List[float], limit: int = 5)` (ARCHITECTURE.md §2, around :37; src/moneta/api.py:378-380). It takes no context, no scopes and no time, and it reads the clock internally (api.py:399).

BLUEPRINT_v7 relies on a read having those inputs in several places:
- :204 defines Resolved(c, n) per context.
- :228 (G2-1) says resolution reads no file and no clock.
- :247-249 says the QueryRecord holds the context and the caller's scopes.
- :434 (P1) says a read depends on (prefix, embedding, limit, context, scopes, t).
- :689 says slot selections depend on the caller's scopes.

At the same time, :80 and X3 (:463) say all four signatures stay unchanged. A search of the paper for caller, session, binding, "per store" and "host passes" finds no statement of how a `query` call obtains `c` or the scopes. The only "host passes" line (:341) is about signal_attention. RULINGS.md has no ruling on context or scopes, and pass1_rulings_brief only says the host logs them (:88). It does not say how the substrate receives them.

The asymmetry the finding points out holds. O14 (:679) sends the write-side echo question to §9, but the read side has no O-item and no Round 4 row. BLUEPRINT_v6.md:95 confirms that v5's `recall` takes context and scopes, so v1's `query` is not v5's read.

The same gap is in `deposit`, which strengthens the finding. The deposit event journals a `scope` (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:134), but the locked `deposit(payload, embedding, protected_floor)` has no scope parameter either. The P1 row tags its claim `[A]` and "false in v1" (:434), but that tag is about decay_all writing on reads. It says nothing about missing parameters, so it does not cover this gap.
verdicts.better_fix:
The direction is right but the fix is incomplete.

(1) Cover both sides. The binding has to supply the scope a `deposit` records (:134) as well as the context and scopes a `query` reads. Otherwise `deposit` has the same gap.

(2) A journaled harness op that binds context and scopes, for example `bind{context, scopes}`, is a new G1 event kind. It must be added to the G1 event table. It must also be classified against the signed set, because granting a caller wider scopes is an authorization act and arguably belongs in the signed set (K3/G1-4). It should also be checked against G2-5, so a binding can't admit scopes the bound context lacks.

(3) State that a `query` at seq n resolves against the binding live at n. Then G2-1 holds, and the QueryRecord's context and scopes become a copy of journaled state, not host-only input. Time still comes from the substrate clock (api.py:399), so the paper must say the echo time is stamped at read, and that this is the only clock read.

(4) If the owner rejects a binding op, the Round 4 row for a context-bearing `query` is the fallback. Add it as O15 next to O14.

(5) Keep V-QUERYSIG, with one change: it should assert the signatures of all four ops, `deposit` included, against ARCHITECTURE.md §2. Also add a sabotage case for it: a hidden module-level context global that the read path consults without journaling it.

all.title: The prescribed open fallback loads exactly the checkpoint that G3-3 and V-HASHGATE forbid
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:390 (§3 Open step 2) vs :294 (G3-3) and :495 (V-HASHGATE)
all.claim: G3-3 says a fold checkpoint 'must also be named by a seal **after the latest rollback**'. V-HASHGATE's pass condition is 'open never uses a checkpoint sealed before the latest rollback', and its sabotage is 'open from a pre-rollback checkpoint'. Open step 2, when the post-rollback reseal isn't attested yet, says to 'load the checkpoint of the latest attested seal **before the rolled-back promote**'. That seal comes before the latest rollback. Counterexample: seal S1 at seq 100, promote g at 110, rollback at 150, reseal S2 at 151 not yet attested. Open loads S1's checkpoint, as the paper prescribes, and V-HASHGATE then flags the correct implementation as sabotaged. Either the fallback or the check has to change.
all.evidence: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:294, :390, :495, :331 (G4-5 reseal)
all.proposed_fix: Reword G3-3 and V-HASHGATE to 'never a checkpoint sealed while any now-RolledBack generation was Promoted'. That matches the safety property step 2 actually relies on. Change the sabotage to 'open from a checkpoint sealed during g's probation'.

verdicts.reason: The contradiction holds when the paper is read as written. G3-3 (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:294) requires a fold checkpoint to be "named by a seal after the latest rollback". V-HASHGATE (:495) passes only if "open never uses a checkpoint sealed before the latest rollback", and its listed sabotage is "open from a pre-rollback checkpoint". Open step 2 (:390) says that when the post-rollback reseal isn't attested yet, open should "load the checkpoint of the latest attested seal before the rolled-back promote". Any seal before the promote is also before the rollback, so in the finding's S1/g/S2 example the prescribed path meets V-HASHGATE's sabotage description word for word. There is one possible escape. G4-5 (:331) says the reseal covers a checkpoint "rebuilt from the last seal before g's promote". If S2 named exactly S1's bytes, G3-3 might be satisfied literally. But S2 is unattested in that scenario, and its checkpoint is a rebuild rather than S1's checkpoint, so the paper doesn't support that reading. Even under it, V-HASHGATE's "sealed before the latest rollback" still fails. The paper doesn't resolve this anywhere. Step 2's last sentence ("Never use a checkpoint sealed while the rolled-back generation was Promoted") already states the property the fix proposes, which shows the author meant that property, but G3-3 and V-HASHGATE weren't brought into line with it. The issue is major because V-HASHGATE is a mile-4 check that would flag a correct implementation.
verdicts.better_fix: Keep the proposed rewording, which matches step 2's own last sentence at :390, and add three things. (1) In G3-3, keep the hash-match requirement for the fallback: the checkpoint's hash must still match the one the attested pre-promote seal names. Also state that the longer tail is folded with G4-5's exclusion of attention stamped with produced_under = g, because otherwise the fallback reintroduces the effects the rollback removed. (2) Split V-HASHGATE's pass condition into two parts: (a) with an attested reseal, open uses the reseal's checkpoint; (b) without one, open uses the latest attested checkpoint sealed outside every RolledBack generation's Promoted interval and folds with exclusions. Use as sabotage both "open from a checkpoint sealed during g's probation" and "fallback that folds the tail without the G4-5 exclusion". (3) Reword G4-5's sentence "The latest seal therefore always follows the latest rollback" (:331) to say "latest seal" in the journal, not "latest attested seal", so it doesn't imply that open can always find an attested post-rollback seal.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute this finding. The contradiction is in the text as written. G3-3 (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:294) requires a fold checkpoint to be "named by a seal **after the latest rollback**". V-HASHGATE (:495) passes only if "open never uses a checkpoint sealed before the latest rollback", and its sabotage is "open from a pre-rollback checkpoint". Open step 2 (:390) has a fallback for when the reseal isn't attested yet: it loads "the checkpoint of the latest attested seal **before the rolled-back promote**". By construction, that seal comes before the latest rollback.

G4-5 (:331) does not reconcile them. It says "the latest seal therefore always follows the latest rollback", but that holds only once the reseal exists. Step 2's fallback is written for exactly the window where the reseal is not attested. The counterexample holds: S1 sealed at seq 100, g promoted at 110, rollback at 150, reseal at 151 unattested. Open loads S1 as step 2 prescribes, and that is the sabotage V-HASHGATE names. The fallback is also semantically sound. The reseal is rebuilt from that same pre-promote seal (G4-5), so loading S1 and folding the longer tail gives the same state.

The proposed fix aims at the right property, but it leaves a gap. It says "sealed while ... was Promoted". Under G4-3/G4-4 and the transitions at :320-322, a generation can also sit in Expired. Expired still has a rollback exit, and g-stamped attention keeps accumulating while g is Expired. A checkpoint sealed while g was Expired would fold g-attributed attention, yet the fix's wording would allow it. Step 2's own last sentence (:390) has the same Promoted-only gap.
verdicts.better_fix:
Use one predicate everywhere: "a checkpoint is usable only if it was sealed while no now-RolledBack generation was in {Promoted, Expired}". Equivalently, it was sealed before that generation's promote or after its rollback. Apply it as follows:

1. **G3-3 (:294).** Replace "named by a seal after the latest rollback" with this predicate. Add that the post-rollback reseal (G4-5) is the preferred checkpoint, and that a pre-promote attested seal is the allowed fallback.
2. **Open step 2 (:390).** Change "while the rolled-back generation was Promoted" to "while any rolled-back generation was Promoted or Expired". State that folding the longer tail applies the G4-5 exclusion.
3. **V-HASHGATE (:495).** Pass condition: "open never uses a checkpoint sealed while a now-RolledBack generation was Promoted or Expired". Sabotage: "open from a checkpoint sealed during g's probation or expiry (after promote, before rollback)".
4. **New V-HASHGATE case.** Add a positive case so the fallback is exercised: reseal unattested, then open from the pre-promote seal and confirm the state equals open from the attested reseal.
5. **G4-5 (:331).** Qualify "the latest seal therefore always follows the latest rollback" with "once the reseal is attested".

all.title: G4 omits roll-forward, and the of edge omits promote and roll-forward, so the signature replay argument fails
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:162, :171-172 (restores/of edges), :307-320 (G4 diagram), :325 (G4-1), :155 and :326 (roll-forward), :500 (V-STATE)
all.claim: (a) G4-1 says 'Only the arrows above exist', but the diagram has no roll-forward arrow. The govern.why table (:155), G4-2, T4 and V-SIGSET all treat roll-forward as a legal transition, so under G4-1 every roll-forward is illegal. (b) :162 claims 'Every adopt, rollback and roll-forward names its target with an **of** edge', but the of edge's source list (:172) is {adopt, rollback, expire, withdraw}. Roll-forward and promote are missing. (c) The replay defense binds the signed body to 'the seq of its of target, or of its restores target'. A promote has neither, so its signed body binds only the genesis hash and the spec. Counterexample: the owner signs promote of spec S (gen g1), then rolls g1 back. The tuner later re-proposes S, which is likely for a deterministic search. The substrate re-appends the old signed promote body: the signature is valid, the transition Proposed→Promoted is legal, and the pointer moves to S without a new owner act. V-STATE's sabotages cover a replayed adopt and a cross-store body, not a replayed promote.
all.evidence: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:162, :172, :307-320, :325, :326, :430, :483, :500; RULINGS.md:21 (R4b promote is owner-signed)
all.proposed_fix: Add `promote → propose` and `roll-forward → (the RolledBack or Retired gen it re-enters)` to the of edge, so every signed body binds a target seq. Add the roll-forward arrow, with its source state, to the G4 diagram. Add 'a promote body replayed onto a later propose of the same spec' as a V-STATE sabotage.

verdicts.reason:
I checked all three parts against the paper and none of them is refuted.

(a) The G4 diagram (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:307-320) has no roll-forward arrow, and no state that roll-forward leaves from or enters. Line 322 lists only adopt and rollback as exits, and G4-1 (:325) says "Only the arrows above exist". Yet roll-forward is listed as a legal, pointer-moving, signed `why` at :155, :326 (G4-2), :430 (T4) and :483 (V-SIGSET). Taken literally, G4-1 makes every roll-forward illegal.

(b) Line :162 says "Every adopt, rollback and roll-forward names its target with an **of** edge". The **of** edge's source set at :172 is {adopt, rollback, expire, withdraw}. Roll-forward and promote are both missing. Roll-forward does carry a `restores` edge (:171), and :162 accepts "or of its restores target" as the binding, so its body still binds a seq. Even so, the sentence about the of edge is false as written.

(c) A promote has no of edge and no restores edge. So by :162 its signed body binds only the genesis hash and the spec. The one other link a promote has is `evidence` (:177), and nowhere does the paper require a promote's evidence hashes to match the current propose. G4-3 (:327) allows at most one Proposed generation, so the substrate can tell which generation a bare promote is meant for. That is what lets the replay land.

The counterexample holds as stated. The owner signs a promote of spec S, then rolls that generation back. The tuner later proposes S again. An old signed body is replayed: the signature checks, and Proposed→Promoted is a legal arrow. V-STATE's sabotages (:500) cover a replayed adopt and a body from another store, not this case. So the claim at :162 that this "rules out replay within a store" fails for promote.

RULINGS.md:21 (R4b) makes promote owner-signed, so the hole sits on a ruled path. Roll-forward's signed status is still pending as O9 (:674, :155). That leaves (a) and the roll-forward half of (b) consistent with the ruling, but they are still internal contradictions in the paper.
verdicts.better_fix:
Adding `promote → propose` to the of edge (:172) fixes the promote replay, because every propose is a fresh, single-use event. Adding the roll-forward arrow and a V-STATE sabotage for "a promote replayed onto a later propose of the same spec" (:500) is also right.

The roll-forward half of the fix does not close replay. A RolledBack or Retired generation can be re-entered more than once, and so can the promote or genesis that a `restores` edge targets. A target seq that can be used again gives no protection. Example: the owner rolls forward to P2, later rolls back to P1, then the old roll-forward body is replayed and the pointer goes back to P2 with no new owner act.

Better fix: make every pointer-moving signed body (promote, adopt, rollback, roll-forward) also bind the seq of the self `govern` live just before it (a "supersedes" or compare-and-swap seq). A body is then valid only against the exact pointer state the owner saw.

Also:
- In the G4 diagram, give roll-forward its source states and its target state.
- Rewrite :162 to match the edge table.
- Add a V-STATE sabotage for a replayed roll-forward after an intervening rollback.

verdicts.reason:
I could not refute any of the three parts against BLUEPRINT_v7.md.

(a) The G4 diagram (:307-320) has no roll-forward arrow. G4-1 (:325) says "Only the arrows above exist". Roll-forward is still listed as pointer-moving and signed in :155, G4-2 (:326), T4 (:430) and V-SIGSET (:483). So the paper contradicts itself, and roll-forward has no legal source state.

(b) :162 says "Every adopt, rollback and roll-forward names its target with an of edge". The of edge at :172 lists only adopt, rollback, expire and withdraw as sources. Roll-forward has only a restores edge (:171). Promote has neither edge, even though of's target set includes promote|propose, which suggests promote→propose was intended.

(c) The binding rule at :162 is "the seq of its of target, or of its restores target". A promote has neither, so its signed body ({tier,name,why,spec,of?}, :139) binds only the genesis hash and the spec. The evidence edges (:177) are hashes outside that listed body. Under P3 a deterministic re-proposal would reproduce the same verdict hash anyway, so evidence would not separate the two promotes. The owner's "Spec ... from exactly one govern" (:201) cannot mean specs are unique, because rollback restores byte-identical specs (T4).

V-STATE's sabotages (:500) cover a replayed adopt and a cross-store body, but not a replayed promote. R4b (RULINGS.md) makes promote owner-signed, so a replayed promote moves the pointer without a new owner act. That is a real gap, and it is major.

The proposed fix is only partly right:
- Promote→propose: correct, and sufficient for promote, because Proposed→Promoted happens once per propose seq.
- Roll-forward: binding it to "the RolledBack or Retired gen it re-enters" adds nothing. That is the same seq as its existing restores target, and a restores target can legitimately be restored many times. The replay survives: the owner rolls forward to g1, a later rollback undoes that, and the old roll-forward body is re-appended. Its signature is valid and the transition is legal. The same weakness applies to any rollback whose of/restores pair can recur.
verdicts.better_fix:
Make every signed pointer-moving body bind a seq that can only be consumed once.
- Promote: add `of: promote → propose`. Every propose seq can be promoted only once, so a replayed promote has nothing left to bind to.
- Roll-forward: set `of` to the specific rollback (or Retired-causing event) it reverses. Add a G4 rule that each such event can be rolled forward at most once.
- Simpler option for all signed pointer moves: put the seq of the live-pointer event (the current head govern for that tier and name) in the signed body. The signature then goes stale as soon as the pointer moves.
- Update :162 to match the of-edge table at :172.
- Add the roll-forward arrow to the G4 diagram, with an explicit source state (RolledBack and/or Retired). The source state depends on O9, which is pending, so flag it for the owner and do not settle it silently.
- Add V-STATE sabotages for both replays:
  1. A promote body re-appended after a later propose of the same spec.
  2. A roll-forward body re-appended after a second rollback.
- State whether the evidence hashes are part of the signed body.

all.title: The v7 retention fold decays at each attention timestamp, a point outside the locked three, but G2-8 is tagged [V] and V-EVAL3 checks only the recall fold
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:235 (G2-8 '[V]'), :283 (retention fold), :492 (V-EVAL3), :634 (mile-0 question row), :672 (O7 attributed to E3)
all.claim: The v7 retention fold runs `u ← decay_value(u, t_last, …, t_event)` and then adds w, once per attention event under the owner's λ. That evaluates stored retention utility at every signal_attention timestamp, before the write. ARCHITECTURE.md §4 locks exactly three points, and point 2 is 'Immediately after the attention-write phase (inside the attention-log reducer)'. v1 does exactly that at reduce time (`attention_log.py:129-131`). The paper's own default therefore adds evaluation points to retention state. Even so, G2-8 asserts '[V]' that stored retention utility is evaluated at exactly three points. V-EVAL3's sabotage checks only that the recall fold doesn't write back, so the retention-fold change has no check. The mile-0 'question' row asks only about the recall fold. O7 sends the order question to E3 (the concurrency lock 3), but the clause it actually overturns is lock 2 (decay math, three evaluation points).
all.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:84-90; CLAUDE.md:35 (lock 2); src/moneta/attention_log.py:108-131; src/moneta/ecs.py:211-214; BLUEPRINT_v7.md:235, :279, :283, :492, :634, :672
all.proposed_fix: Downgrade G2-8 to [P]/[A] for retention under the v7 default. Extend the mile-0 'fourth evaluation point' row to cover the per-event retention fold and cite lock 2, not only E3. Add a V-EVAL3 arm, with its sabotage, that counts retention-utility decay evaluations in a fold and compares them to the three locked sites.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds. BLUEPRINT_v7.md:283 sets the v7 retention fold to apply decay_value(u, t_last, ..., t_event) and then add w, once per event under the owner's λ. That decays stored retention utility at every attention timestamp, before the write. ARCHITECTURE.md:86-88 locks point 2 as 'Immediately after the attention-write phase (inside the attention-log reducer)', and v1 matches it: apply_attention first, then decay_all (attention_log.py:129-131; ecs.py:211-214). The paper sees the order difference (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:279-281) and parks it as O7 (:672). Two problems remain. (1) O7 and its mile-0 row (:634, E3 'retention fold order decided') send it to E3/lock 3, the concurrency clause. The clause it actually strains is §4/lock 2 (ARCHITECTURE.md:84-90; CLAUDE.md lock 2). The mile-0 'question' row (:636) and O2 (:667) cover only the recall fold. (2) G2-8 (:235) tags 'stored retention utility is evaluated at exactly the locked three points' as [V]. Per the legend at :9, [V] means only that v1 source or ARCHITECTURE.md was read. That verifies v1, not the v7 default, which changes the retention-utility evaluation order. V-EVAL3 (:492) has only one sabotage, a recall fold writing anchors back, so nothing checks the retention-fold placement. RULINGS.md has no ruling on fold order: its only retention-fold ruling is the rollback exclusion at :20. So nothing here reopens an owner ruling.

One nuance softens the claim. If the per-event fold runs inside the reducer, the number of call sites stays at three. ARCHITECTURE.md:90's 'test asserts the absence of a fourth call site' would not fire. The real conflict is with point 2's 'after the attention-write phase' wording: decay at t_event before each add, rather than one decay after the batch write. That is still a locked-clause question for the owner, not a local call, so the finding stands as major and needs the owner.
verdicts.better_fix:
The fix is mostly right but aims the test at the wrong thing. Use these changes instead.

(a) Split G2-8's tag. Keep '[V] for v1 (ARCHITECTURE.md:84-90; attention_log.py:129-131)'. Mark the v7 default retention fold '[P], pending O7'. Note that the per-event order decays before each write, while point 2 is worded 'after the attention-write phase'.

(b) Retarget O7 and the E3 mile-0 cell (:634, :672) to cite ARCHITECTURE.md §4:84-90 / CLAUDE.md lock 2 as the clause at stake, and keep E3 only as the venue. Extend the mile-0 'question' row (:636), or O2, to ask whether a per-event retention fold inside the reducer satisfies 'immediately after the attention-write phase'.

(c) Don't add a V-EVAL3 arm that counts call sites. A fold inside the reducer keeps three call sites, so the arm would pass while the conflict stands. Make the arm assert the evaluation order and timestamps instead: retention utility is decayed only at a reduce/query/sleep 'now', after the batch write. Under the v7 default, that arm is expected to fail until Round 4 rules. Pair it with the existing per-event vs per-batch fixture in V-ORACLE-FOLD (:285). The sabotage: a retention fold that decays at t_event before the add, while G2-8 still claims v1 semantics.

verdicts.reason:
The finding stands. ARCHITECTURE.md:84-90 locks exactly three evaluation points. Point 2 is "Immediately after the attention-write phase (inside the attention-log reducer)", and :90 says "No fourth evaluation point". v1 matches this: it decays once, at reduce time `now`, after the batch write (src/moneta/attention_log.py:129-131; ecs.py:211-214 sets _last_evaluated=now). The paper documents v1's behavior itself (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:272-279).

The v7 retention fold departs from that. BLUEPRINT_v7.md:283 sets "the same per-event order under the owner's λ" as the [P] default, and :282 defines that order as decay_value(u, t_last, ..., t_event) and then add w. That evaluates stored retention utility at every attention timestamp, before the write, not once after the write phase.

G2-8 (:235) still tags "exactly the locked three points" [V] for stored retention utility. Only the recall fold gets [P] and goes to O2. V-EVAL3 (:492) has a single sabotage, a recall fold writing back, so the retention-fold change has no check. The mile-0 question row (:634) and O2 (:667) both ask only about the recall fold.

The paper does notice the step-order question. O7 (:672) and :283 send it to Round 4 under E3. But E3's lock is CLAUDE.md lock 3 and §5.1 (concurrency and the ordered journal, :631). It never says the per-event order touches lock 2 or §4 (:630 cites §4 only for E2, reads never write). So the paper handles this as an ordering question, not an evaluation-point question.

The strongest counter is weak. One could argue per-event decay happens "inside the attention-log reducer", which matches point 2's location clause. It still breaks the timing clause, "immediately after the attention-write phase", and it raises the number of decay evaluations per batch from 1 to N. At best the reading is ambiguous, which is exactly the owner/Round 4 question the finding asks to surface. The [V] tag is also defensible only for v1 at 6cf05f5, and the sentence is written about the v7 design.

Severity major is fair. It is an unflagged collision with a CLAUDE.md "do not re-open" lock in the paper's own default.
verdicts.better_fix:
The direction is correct. I would refine three parts.

(1) Don't downgrade G2-8 wholesale; split it. Keep "v1 evaluates stored retention utility at exactly three points [V, attention_log.py:129-131, api.py:401, sleep pass]". Then add "under v7's declared per-event retention fold (:283), stored retention utility is evaluated at each attention timestamp before the write; whether that is point 2 or a fourth point is open [P], O2/O7".

(2) Widen O2 and the mile-0 question row (:634) to cover both folds. Cite ARCHITECTURE.md:87 and :90 and CLAUDE.md lock 2 alongside E3. In O7 (:672), say that lock 2 is in play as well as lock 3. Add a "v1's per-batch order" outcome as the lock-2-safe fallback.

(3) The new V-EVAL3 arm should be conditional on the Round 4 ruling. As written ("count decay evaluations and compare to three sites"), it fails by construction under the paper's own per-event default. Specify both forms:
- If per-event is ruled to be point 2: assert that every retention decay call sits inside the reducer and that none sits outside the three sites. Sabotage: a decay call in signal_attention or on a timer.
- If per-batch is ruled: assert exactly one retention decay per reduce, at `now` after the write. Sabotage: the per-event decay.

Also fix V-ORACLE-FOLD's sabotage (:284) so it matches whichever order is ruled.

all.title: If E3 is rejected, ruled R4a has nowhere to live, and the mile-0 table neither says so nor gives a kill or rescope
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:631 (E3 'if ruled against'), :641-646 (Kill list), :135 and :174 (attention node and produced_under edge), :499, :503-504, :524
all.claim: E3's against-branch says only 'the journal and the attention log coexist; their relative order becomes an open risk'. But R4a (ruled) is realized entirely through `attention` being a G1 event with a seq: the `gen` stamp (:135), the produced_under edge (:174), G4-5's exclusion, V-GENTAG, V-LEAK, V-EXCL and the V-UNDO sabotage. If Round 4 keeps the locked §5.1 log, which is drained and cleared at every sleep pass (ARCHITECTURE.md:106, :110), attention leaves no durable seq'd record. A later rollback then has nothing to exclude from utility or `attended_count`, and R4a can't be implemented. The kill list covers E1, E2, E4 and the half-life call, but not E3.
all.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:106, :110-112; CLAUDE.md:36 (lock 3); RULINGS.md:20 (R4a); BLUEPRINT_v7.md:135, :174, :329-331, :631, :641-646
all.proposed_fix: Change E3's against-branch to 'R4a cannot be implemented as ruled: either attention gets a durable, seq'd, gen-stamped side record (which is itself a §5.1 change), or R4 falls back to shadow-only'. Add 'E3 rejected → rescope R4a or shadow-only' to the Kill list. Tell the owner that ruling R4a in effect pre-commits Round 4 on E3.

verdicts.reason: The finding stands. In BLUEPRINT_v7.md, attention exists only as a G1 journal node: `attention` carries the `gen` stamp (:135), the produced_under edge runs from it (:174), and G1-3 checks it (:187). Everything R4a needs is built on that seq'd event: the retention-fold exclusion (:330), J8 (:452), V-LEAK (:499), the V-UNDO sabotage (:503), V-GENTAG (:504) and V-EXCL (:524). E3's against-branch (:631) says only 'the journal and the attention log coexist; their relative order becomes an open risk'. It never says where the gen-stamped attention lives, or whether R4a survives. The Kill list (:641-646) covers E1, E2, E4, the half-life call and record loss, but not E3. The locks table (:611) and O7 (:672) also leave the E3-rejected case unaddressed. The locked §5.1 (ARCHITECTURE.md:106, :110) has the sleep pass apply the log and then clear it. v1 entries are (entity_id, weight, timestamp) with no generation (blueprint :341, citing attention_log.py:73). Utility and attended_count are mutated in place (consolidation.py:111-112 and ecs.py:213, both cited in the paper). So once a sleep pass runs, no record is left to exclude later. One overstatement: R4a is not strictly unimplementable without the journal. The paper's own G4 hold (:293) says probation attention is kept from retention until adopt or rollback. A §5.1 log that carried a gen field and held probation-stamped entries across sleep passes, dropping them on rollback, would satisfy R4a. But that still changes the locked 'reads the log, applies, then clears' rule. It also needs a schema change to the log entries. So the core claim holds: rejecting E3 takes away R4a's mechanism unless §5.1 is amended anyway. Severity major is fair: R4a is ruled, R4 runs shadow-only through mile 4 (:621), and the gap would surface at mile 5's V-UNDO (:657). This is not a request to reopen R4a. It shows a consequence of the ruling, which RULINGS permits.
verdicts.better_fix: Keep the direction of the proposed fix with three refinements. (1) E3 'if ruled against' (:631) should read: 'R4a has no carrier. Either Round 4 also amends §5.1 so the attention log carries the `gen` stamp and probation-stamped entries are held across sleep passes until adopt or rollback (the G4 hold, :293), or attention is mirrored into a durable, seq'd, gen-stamped side record. Both are §5.1 changes. Otherwise R4 stays shadow_only past mile 4.' Also replace 'their relative order becomes an open risk' with a named O-item, because V-GENTAG's 'live at its seq' (:504) is undefined without a shared order. (2) Add to the Kill list (:641-646): 'E3 rejected without a §5.1 amendment carrying the gen stamp: R4 stays shadow_only (R4a not implementable); V-UNDO, V-LEAK, V-GENTAG and V-EXCL are struck from miles 4–5.' (3) Soften the owner note from 'pre-commits Round 4 on E3' to 'ruling R4a means Round 4 must either accept E3 or amend §5.1's clear-at-sleep-pass rule; the Round 4 brief should say so'. Also update the §7 locks row (:611) to match.

verdicts.reason:
The gap is real and nothing in the paper fills it.

- **E3's against-branch** (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:631) says only that the journal and the attention log coexist and that their order becomes an open risk. It never mentions R4a.
- **The Kill list** (:641-646) covers E4, E2, E1, the half-life call and record loss. It has no E3 entry.
- **R4a depends on the journal.** It is ruled in RULINGS.md:20, and it rests entirely on `attention` being a seq'd G1 event with a `gen` stamp: the node at :135, the produced_under edge at :174, G4-5 at :329-331, and V-GENTAG, V-LEAK, V-EXCL and V-UNDO at :499-524.
- **The paper says this in its own words** at :611: the attention log is "Replaced by the journal under E3 [A]".
- **v1 log entries carry no generation.** They hold only `(entity_id, weight, timestamp)` (:341, attention_log.py:73).
- **The locked §5.1 log is cleared at every sleep pass** (ARCHITECTURE.md:106, :110). So without E3, nothing recorded can tell which attention a fold must drop after a rollback.
- **Other places where E3 appears don't fill the gap.** :283 and O7 (:672) mention E3 only for fold step order. Q10 (:591) covers only GIL independence.

One part of the claim goes too far. "Coexist" could mean dual-write: attention appended as a G1 event with a `gen` stamp, while the v1 log still feeds the ECS reducer. In that case R4a is not strictly impossible. But the retention fold would then have to read the journal, or log entries would need a `gen` tag. Either is a §5.1 change Round 4 would have to rule on, and the paper says none of this. So the finding stands at major severity.
verdicts.better_fix:
Mostly right. Three changes would sharpen it.

1. **Name the dual-write option in E3's against-branch.** Suggested text: "R4a is implementable only if (i) attention is also appended as a seq'd, gen-stamped G1 event and the retention fold reads the journal, not the drained log, or (ii) v1 log entries gain a `gen` tag and the log is not cleared under a G4-4 hold. Both change §5.1 and must be put to Round 4. Otherwise R4 runs shadow-only for good, which makes R4a moot because nothing on a real store is ever promoted or rolled back."
2. **Add a Kill-list line:** "E3 rejected without (i) or (ii): R4 is fixed at shadow_only and miles 5–6 are rescoped."
3. **Soften the owner note.** Replace "pre-commits Round 4 on E3" with: "R4a, as ruled, depends on E3 or on a §5.1 amendment. The Round 4 brief should say so explicitly, so the reviewers know that rejecting E3 also turns R4 into shadow-only."

all.title: J7's indefinite hold suspends the locked §6 MAX_ENTITIES consolidation trigger, and the locks table doesn't list it
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:328 (G4-4), :333-339 (G4-7: Expired keeps the hold with no time limit), :451 (J7), :607-615 (locks table)
all.claim: G4-4 forbids every `retention` event while a generation is Promoted or Expired. Expired has no time-out: it ends only on a signed adopt or rollback, and the O5 default is hold plus an alarm. ARCHITECTURE.md §6 sets consolidation triggers, including pressure when the volatile count exceeds MAX_ENTITIES (ruling #5, `consolidation.py:8,49,88`), and §15.7 keeps §2–§10 in force. Counterexample: promote g, wait past the 14-day ceiling, and the owner is offline. Deposits keep arriving, the volatile count passes 10,000, and the sleep pass that §6 requires can't prune or stage. The locks table (:607-615) lists every other overturned lock but not §6's triggers. Attack #7 asks only about §15.2 rotation.
all.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:120-123, :323; src/moneta/consolidation.py:8, :49, :88; BLUEPRINT_v7.md:328, :333-339, :607-615, :692
all.proposed_fix: Add a locks-table row: '§6 pressure trigger: suspended during probation and Expired; Round 4'. Alternatively, add an X1 cap on hold duration or entity growth, past which the substrate forces the O5 decision. Then add a V-HOLD arm that crosses MAX_ENTITIES during a hold.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds, and I found nothing in the paper that handles it.

1. **The hold has no end in time.** G4-4 (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:328) forbids any `retention` event while a generation is in {Promoted, Expired}. J7 (:451) says this means sleep passes are held. G4-7 (:333-339) keeps the hold when the ceiling is reached, with an alarm and no time limit, and only a signed adopt or rollback ends Expired (:322). O5 (:670) makes that the default.

2. **The suspended trigger is locked.** ARCHITECTURE.md:120-123 (§6) names the trigger "ECS volatile count exceeds `MAX_ENTITIES`". §15.7 (ARCHITECTURE.md:323) keeps §2–§10 in force. The code agrees: `consolidation.py:8` and `:49` set the default to 10000 (ruling #5), and `should_run` at `:88` fires the pass on pressure.

3. **The paper never deals with the conflict.** Grepping the blueprint for MAX_ENTITIES, "pressure" and "§6 trigger" finds nothing:
   - The locks table (:607-615) has no row for §6's triggers.
   - The E4 table (:632) covers §6 prune *semantics* only. It does not cover trigger suspension.
   - Attack #7 (:692) asks only about §15.2 rotation.
   - V-HOLD (:502) checks only that no sleep pass runs, so it would mark the trigger's suppression green.

4. **The finding understates its own scope.** The trigger is suspended during ordinary probation too, which lasts up to 14 days or the X1 maximum, not only in Expired. With high deposit volume, the count can pass MAX_ENTITIES before the ceiling is reached.

5. **One overstatement, which doesn't change the result.** "Lists every other overturned lock" is too strong. The locks table mirrors the CLAUDE.md headline locks, and E4 sits in a separate table, so the omission is a missing row and a missing attack, not an inconsistency inside the table. The §6 trigger is still locked through §15.7, and v7 suspends it without saying so.

6. **Not a reopened ruling.** J7 is tagged `[P]`, not RULED (:451), so raising this doesn't reopen anything the owner has ruled. R4c ruled one pending generation plus a ceiling with a default. The pressure-trigger consequence is the kind of thing the owner should know before deciding O5.

The finding is correct, needs the owner, and major is about the right severity.
verdicts.better_fix:
The proposed fix points the right way but leaves gaps:

- the row should cover probation, not only Expired;
- it should name §15.7, since that is what makes §6 locked;
- the cap has to say what happens when it is reached.

**Recommended edits:**

1. **Locks table (:607-615).** Add a row: "§6 consolidation triggers (MAX_ENTITIES pressure, idle > 5000 ms; ARCHITECTURE.md:120-123, locked by §15.7 :323; `consolidation.py:49,88`) | Suspended for the whole Promoted+Expired hold under J7/G4-4. Expired's hold has no time limit. Needs Round 4 (§9 Trigger 2)."

2. **New invariant G4-8 (Pressure under hold).** It gives the owner two options for O5:
   - **(a) Bound the hold by entity count.** Add an X1 constitution cap, for example a ceiling on volatile count, past which the substrate forces the O5 decision (escalating alarm, then auto-rollback if the owner has chosen that).
   - **(b) Let pressure passes run during the hold.** Pressure-triggered sleep passes run, but the retention fold excludes every `attention` event whose `produced_under` points to the pending generation. This is the G4-5 rule applied in advance. The pass can't take on the pending generation's influence, and the pressure trigger stays alive.

   Under (b), J7 changes from "no sleep pass" to "no pending-gen attention reaches retention". If the generation is later adopted, attention that was excluded from pruned entities can't be restored, and E4's tombstone semantics bear on whether that loss is acceptable. Record that under O5.

3. **V-HOLD (:502).** Add an arm in which deposits push the volatile count past MAX_ENTITIES during probation and during Expired. Under the chosen option, the arm checks either the forced decision or a pressure pass that carries no pending-gen attention. The sabotage case is a store that grows without bound while the hold is in place.

4. **Attack #7 (:692).** Widen it to cover §6's pressure trigger as well as §15.2 rotation.

verdicts.reason: The finding stands. G4-4 (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:328) forbids every `retention` event while a generation is in {Promoted, Expired}. Line :136 defines a `retention` event as "tombstone and stage decisions from a sleep pass", so the hold stops both of §6's selection outputs. G4-7 (:333-339) keeps the hold in Expired, and Expired has only two exits, both owner-signed (:322). O5 (:670) defaults to hold plus an alarm, so nothing bounds how long the hold lasts. ARCHITECTURE.md:120-123 makes "ECS volatile count exceeds MAX_ENTITIES" a consolidation trigger. Code implements it at consolidation.py:8, :49 (default 10000, ruling #5) and :88. ARCHITECTURE.md:3 marks the whole document LOCKED, and §15.7 (:323) keeps §2–§10 in force. The paper never mentions MAX_ENTITIES or the pressure trigger: a grep for MAX_ENTITIES and "pressure" in BLUEPRINT_v7.md returns nothing. Attack 7 (:692) asks only how the hold interacts with §15.2 rotation, not with §6 memory pressure. The Round-4 overturn table (:627-634) lists §6 prune semantics as E4 but not the trigger being suspended. V-HOLD (:502) checks only that no retention event appears; no arm grows past MAX_ENTITIES during a hold. Two points weaken the finding without refuting it. (1) The §6 heading carries no "(locked)" tag, unlike §2–§5 and §7–§10, and the trigger is not one of CLAUDE.md's five locked decisions. It is locked only through the doc-wide LOCKED status at :3 and §15.7, so "locked" holds, though less strongly than the finding implies. Also, the locks table at :607-615 does not list "every other overturned lock": E4 sits in the Round-4 table instead. (2) G4-6 (:332) keeps real stores in Proposed through mile 4, so the issue first bites at mile 5 (:657). Severity is therefore major for mile 5 and later, not for the near-term miles. J7 is tagged [P], not RULED, so raising it reopens no owner ruling.
verdicts.better_fix: The direction is right, but two parts need changing. (a) Put the row where overturned ARCHITECTURE clauses are tracked: the Round-4 overturn table (:627-634), next to E4. For example: "§6 pressure trigger (ARCHITECTURE.md:120-121; consolidation.py:88) is suspended for retention while a generation is in {Promoted, Expired}; v1 line consolidation.py:88; ruled for → hold as drawn plus a growth policy; ruled against → J7 narrows." A cross-reference line in §7 Locks is enough there. (b) The alternative 'X1 cap past which the substrate forces the O5 decision' is wrong as written. A substrate-forced pointer move without a signature breaks J6/G4-2, which is RULED (R4). Any auto-rollback has to stay the O5 carve-out that the owner rules on. Recast it as a new owner question, or as an extension of O5: when the volatile count crosses MAX_ENTITIES during a hold, choose between (i) raising the alarm and refusing or back-pressuring deposits, (ii) a signed auto-rollback carve-out, or (iii) staging-only consolidation exempt from the hold. Option (iii) needs a statement of whether staging can carry the generation's influence. Also widen attack 7 (:692) to include §6 memory pressure. Keep the V-HOLD arm: grow past MAX_ENTITIES during Expired, and assert the chosen policy, the alarm, and that no retention event appears.

all.title: G3-8 claims §15.2 is kept but has no check and omits constraint #4 (shadow commit ≤ 15 ms p99)
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:299 (G3-8), :613 (locks table 'Untouched'), §5 check table :475-525
all.claim: G3-8 is the only invariant that carries CLAUDE.md lock 5, yet no V-* check cites it. That breaks the paper's own rule that 'every check is that invariant plus the sabotage it must catch' (:39) and that every rule has a check. It also lists only constraints 1–3 (ARCHITECTURE.md:271-273) plus ChangeBlock. Constraint #4, the shadow commit budget of ≤ 15 ms p99 (ARCHITECTURE.md:274), is dropped. That matters because v7 turns the vector index into a content-addressed derived leaf (:262, :378) and adds a payload file write per deposit (:376). Either change can move the commit cost the locked budget governs. 'Untouched' (:613) is therefore asserted, not checked.
all.evidence: ARCHITECTURE.md:271-274; CLAUDE.md:38; BLUEPRINT_v7.md:39, :262, :299, :376, :613
all.proposed_fix: Add V-ENVELOPE (G3-8): rotation at 50k, idle > 5 s, ≤ 500-prim batches, and shadow commit ≤ 15 ms p99 measured on the v7 deposit path. Sabotages: a policy-layer regeneration routed through the record batch path, and the per-deposit payload write left out of the commit timing. Add constraint #4 to G3-8.

verdicts.reason:
The main claim holds. Every check row cites its invariants in the second column, and none of the rows at BLUEPRINT_v7.md:477-525 cites G3-8. The only G3-8 references are its definition (:299) and the locks table (:613). So the §15.2 envelope has no check, and "Untouched" (:613) is asserted, not tested. That conflicts with :39, "Every check is that invariant plus the sabotage it must catch."

The part about constraint #4 is weaker than stated. The paper did not drop it silently. Under "The cost to name" (:592-599) it notes that v1 has no LanceDB (vector_index.py:35-44, pyproject.toml:37), calls ARCHITECTURE.md:274's LanceDB commit budget "a docs/code drift for the Documentarian, not a v7 decision", and leaves it out of G3-8 on purpose.

That handling is still flawed, and the owner should know why. CLAUDE.md:38 names the "15ms shadow commit budget" as part of locked decision 5, and CLAUDE.md:40 says a reason a lock looks wrong is a §9 Trigger 2, not a local fix. Downgrading a locked budget to "drift" without escalating, while the locks table (:613) says §15.2 is "Untouched", contradicts the paper's own lock accounting. The atomicity lock gets this treatment correctly (:611, "Superseded by E1 [A]. Needs Round 4"). The envelope row should say the same about #4, or G3-8 should carry it.

So: no check for G3-8 is confirmed. "#4 omitted" is confirmed in G3-8 and :613, but it is a deliberate, though mis-classified, exclusion rather than an oversight.
verdicts.better_fix:
The V-ENVELOPE half is right; keep it. Add a check row citing G3-8 that asserts rotation at 50k prims, consolidation only in idle windows over 5 s, batches of at most 500 prims, and every record-projection write inside one Sdf.ChangeBlock (ARCHITECTURE.md:271-273, convention #5). Sabotages: a policy-layer or cortex-projection regeneration routed through the record batch path, and a batch larger than 500 or a write outside a ChangeBlock. Assign it a mile.

Change the constraint #4 half. Re-aiming the 15 ms p99 budget at "the v7 deposit path including the payload write" invents a new budget for a different operation, and that is itself a lock change. ARCHITECTURE.md:274 governs the LanceDB shadow commit (the vector-index write in the USD-first, vector-second sequence), which v7 replaces with a content-addressed derived leaf and E1.

Instead, make G3-8 and the :613 row say explicitly that constraint #4 is not carried. The v7 vector index is a derived leaf (:262, :378) under E1 `[A]`, so whether a commit budget applies to the journal append plus payload write goes to Round 4 with E1, the same way the atomicity lock at :611 does. Change :613 from "Untouched" to "Kept for #1–3 and ChangeBlock (G3-8, V-ENVELOPE); #4 superseded with E1, needs Round 4". Keep the :596-599 drift note, but cross-reference the lock instead of calling it purely a Documentarian matter. If the owner wants a latency guard anyway, put a measured but unlocked p99 for the journal append in the mile-4 exit criteria, labelled `[U]`, not presented as the §15.2 number.

verdicts.reason: The finding holds. G3-8 (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:299) lists only constraints 1–3 (ARCHITECTURE.md:271-273) plus ChangeBlock. No row in the §5 check table (:475-525) cites G3-8; the table goes from V-LEAF/V-NOFEEDBACK/V-HASHGATE/V-REBUILD (G3-1..5) to V-HOLDOUT (G3-6) and V-LEAK (G3-7) and stops there. That breaks the rule at :39 ("Every rule is an invariant of one graph. Every check is that invariant plus the sabotage it must catch") and the mile-4 gate at :655 ("every §5 check..."). The locks table row at :613 says §15.2 is "Untouched", but no check backs that, and constraint #4 (ARCHITECTURE.md:274, LanceDB shadow commit ≤ 15 ms p99) is missing from G3-8. The only nearby defence is §6 "The cost to name" (:593-599), which flags ARCHITECTURE.md:274 as "a docs/code drift for the Documentarian, not a v7 decision". That does not settle it. It is never cross-referenced from G3-8 or from :613. Dropping one of the seven locked hard constraints (CLAUDE.md lock 5) should be an explicit disposition, not something implied by a docs-drift note. So "Untouched" is still asserted, not shown. Severity "minor" is fair. One factual nuance: §15.2 #4 is a LanceDB budget, v1 has no LanceDB (:593), and v7 makes the vector index a derived leaf (:262, :378). The "shadow commit" the budget governs may therefore not exist on the v7 deposit path at all. That makes the fix's measurement target wrong, though the gap itself is real.
verdicts.better_fix: Keep the V-ENVELOPE check for constraints 1–3 with these sabotages: a policy-layer regeneration routed through the 500-prim record batch path (it contradicts :407); a consolidation batch over 500 prims; rotation skipped past 50k; consolidation run outside an idle window of more than 5 s, e.g. on a tick. Do not tell implementers to measure "shadow commit ≤ 15 ms p99 on the v7 deposit path". The 15 ms is a LanceDB shadow-commit budget (ARCHITECTURE.md:274), and v1/v7 have no LanceDB commit (:593); in v7 the vector index is a derived leaf rebuilt off the journal. Instead, give constraint #4 an explicit disposition in G3-8 and in the :613 row, cross-referenced to §6 "The cost to name" (:593-599). Two options: (a) dormant, because no LanceDB shadow commit exists in v1 or v7, with the vector-index leaf kept off the deposit path and that fact checked; or (b) re-targeted to whatever synchronous work v7 adds per deposit (the payloads/<sha256> write at :376, any leaf update), with a recorded budget. If (b) changes a locked number, raise it as a ruling or a §9 note for the owner. Change "Untouched" to "1–3 kept and checked (V-ENVELOPE); #4 disposition per G3-8".

all.title: Contradictions: adopt is both 'pointer-moving' and 'moves nothing', and the loop can cause more than one node kind
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:154 vs :326; :61 vs :327 and :484
all.claim: (a) The govern.why table says `adopt` moves the pointer or policy 'no. It ends probation' (:154). G4-2 lists adopt among 'pointer-moving edge (promote, adopt, rollback, roll-forward)' (:326). V-STATE's 'moves nothing' assertion covers propose, withdraw and expire, so it's undefined which property is checked for adopt. (b) 'On one screen' says the loop can cause 'exactly one node kind' to be added, an unsigned propose (:61). But G4-3 makes a new propose trigger a substrate `withdraw` of the pending Proposed generation (:327), and V-WRITE permits it (:484). A loop proposal can therefore withdraw a proposal the owner is reviewing, and the paper's own line doesn't account for that.
all.proposed_fix: Define 'moves' once (the policy pointer vs the G4 state) and make the table and G4-2 agree. Restate the line as 'propose, and the withdraw it implies', or forbid a new propose while one is Proposed instead of auto-withdrawing.

verdicts.reason: Both parts hold against the text. (a) The govern.why table (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:146-154) has the column "moves the pointer or policy?", and its row for `adopt` says "no. It ends probation" (:154). G4-2 (:326) names adopt among the "pointer-moving edge (promote, adopt, rollback, roll-forward)", and the J2-15 fix (:810) depends on that split: "G4-2 covers pointer-moving edges; unsigned edges move nothing". V-STATE (:500) checks that propose, withdraw and expire move nothing. It never says which property it checks for adopt. The paper uses "moves" for two things, the policy pointer and the G4 generation state, and never defines it. (b) Line :61 says the loop can cause "exactly one node kind to be added to G1", the unsigned propose. But G4-3 (:327) says a new propose while one is Proposed "is preceded by a substrate `withdraw` of the old one". V-WRITE (:484) allows "(the substrate may add `withdraw`)", and the table (:152) admits a withdraw can come from "a newer proposal replaced". So the loop's propose does cause a second node kind. The line's principle still holds, because withdraw is unsigned and moves no policy. The wording "exactly one node kind" is still wrong. Partial handling at :152 and :484 does not fix :61, so this is not refuted. One consequence the finding understates: the owner reviews a Proposed generation and signs `promote` off-machine (:416). The signed body binds the `seq` of its target (:162). If a loop propose withdraws that generation mid-review, the owner's signed promote targets a Withdrawn generation and is refused. R4c (RULINGS.md:22) only requires "one pending", so it allows either auto-withdraw or refusal. Choosing between them is a design choice, not a reopened ruling.
verdicts.better_fix: Define the two terms once, near :146. "Policy pointer" means the live self generation that resolution uses. "G4 state" means the generation lifecycle. Then rename the table column to "moves the policy pointer?", keep adopt at "no (ends probation; G4 state change)", and reword G4-2 to "every edge that moves the policy pointer or ends a pending generation (promote, adopt, rollback, roll-forward) is owner-signed". V-STATE then asserts both: propose, withdraw and expire change neither, and adopt changes G4 state only. For (b), the better choice is to refuse a new loop propose while one is Proposed, instead of auto-withdrawing. That keeps :61 literally true and means a loop can never invalidate a promote the owner is signing off-machine (:162, :416). Withdraw then comes only from the owner declining or from an expiry or timeout rule. If auto-withdraw stays, restate :61 as "an unsigned propose, plus the unsigned substrate withdraw of any proposal it replaces". Also add a V-STATE case for a signed promote whose `of` target was withdrawn by replacement: it must be refused, and the refusal must be reported to the owner.

verdicts.reason: Both halves hold against the text. (a) The govern.why table header at BLUEPRINT_v7.md:147 asks "moves the pointer or policy?", and the adopt row at :154 answers "no. It ends probation". G4-2 at :326 lists adopt among the "pointer-moving edge (promote, adopt, rollback, roll-forward)". Those two lines contradict each other. RULINGS.md:21 (R4b) only says adopt is owner-signed, which both lines respect, so the conflict is in the paper's own definition of "moves", not in the ruling. The finding's point that V-STATE (:500) has no moves-property for adopt is weaker: V-SIGSET (:485) covers adopt's signature, and V-STATE doesn't need a moves check for it. That sub-point is a side note, but the contradiction stands. (b) :61 says the loop "can cause exactly one node kind to be added to G1", an unsigned propose. G4-3 (:327) makes a new propose while one is Proposed be "preceded by a substrate withdraw of the old one". V-WRITE (:484) says "the substrate may add withdraw", and the withdraw row (:152) names "a newer proposal replaced" as a cause. So a loop action does cause a second node kind, and it can end a proposal the owner is reviewing at step 7 (:416). The line's underlying guarantee still holds, because withdraw is unsigned and moves nothing (:152, :326). The "exactly one node kind" wording is still literally false. Nothing in the paper reconciles these lines, and RULINGS.md:22 (R4c, "only one generation may be pending") does not decide the matter: the paper's own G4-3 already separates pending ({Promoted, Expired}) from Proposed, and R4c does not require auto-withdraw. Minor severity is right.
verdicts.better_fix: The fix works. A tighter wording that leaves every ruling intact: (1) Rename G4-2 to "Signed state-changing edges (promote, adopt, rollback, roll-forward)". Keep the table at :154 as is, since adopt changes G4 state and does not move the policy pointer. Add one sentence defining "moves" as moving the policy pointer, and make the table header, G4-2 and V-STATE use that single meaning. (2) Restate :61 as: "the loop can cause exactly one node kind to be added: an unsigned govern{why: propose}, plus, when it replaces a pending proposal, the substrate's unsigned withdraw of that proposal. Neither changes policy." This keeps the line's guarantee, because neither event moves the pointer. Picking between auto-withdraw and refusing a new propose while one is Proposed is a design choice that R4c does not settle. If the paper switches to refusal, it should flag the change as an [P] proposal, because refusal changes the loop's cadence and owner review timing at :416. Then V-WRITE (:484) and the withdraw row (:152) need updating to match.

all.title: Mile-3 checks depend on artifacts that only exist at mile 4
all.location: BLUEPRINT_v7.md:496 (V-REBUILD, mile 3), :516 (V-REPLAY, mile 3), :654 (mile 3 done-means), :655 (mile 4 builds format 7, the G1 chain and leaves)
all.claim: V-REPLAY's pass condition is 'reproduces every **journaled** `propose` verdict', and V-REBUILD requires 'the eval set and **every leaf**' to rebuild byte-identically. Both are required green 'on a real store' at mile 3. But the format-7 journal, `govern{propose}` events and the G3 leaves (fold checkpoints, USD policy layers) are built only at mile 4 ('The graphs in the store', :655). At mile 3 no journaled propose and no checkpoint leaf exists, so both checks are vacuous or can't be run, and mile 3's done-means can't be met as written.
all.proposed_fix: Split them: at mile 3, V-REPLAY covers shadow-logged verdicts and V-REBUILD covers only the eval set. Move the journaled-propose and all-leaves arms to mile 4.

verdicts.reason:
I couldn't refute this; the finding holds. The paper sets V-REBUILD to mile 3 (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:496): "the eval set and every leaf rebuild byte-identically". It sets V-REPLAY to mile 3 as well (:516): "reproduces every journaled `propose` verdict". Mile 3's done-means (:654) requires both green "on a real store". The things they test do not exist until later:
(1) `propose` becomes a journaled `govern{why: propose}` event only as a format-7 change (:114). The fix log says unjournaled shadow records were deliberately replaced by journaled `propose` (:792, J1-7/J2-9). Mile 4 is the first mile to build format 7 and the G1 chain (:655). The pass-1 brief agrees that "mile 4 builds the `govern` and `seal` edges" and that mile 3 only adds query-log nodes (pass1_rulings_brief.md:396).
(2) The G3 leaves listed at :261 and :378 are fold checkpoints named by `seal` events (:140, :175), the vector index, recall anchors and USD policy layers. Seals and G2 derived USD are mile-4 items (:655). Mile 3 only adds "the G3 eval-set builder" (:654).
So at mile 3 the journaled-propose arm of V-REPLAY has nothing to test, and the "every leaf" arm of V-REBUILD can't be met. Nothing in the paper resolves this. Other checks do split by mile, such as V-HOLDOUT "2 (simulated) / 3" at :497 and V-SIGSET "4 / 5" at :483, but these two have no split. The same problem also affects V-SHADOW (:506, "3–4"): "leaves Proposed" assumes the G4 machine and journaled `propose`, and both arrive at mile 4. Minor severity is right: this is a mile-scheduling inconsistency, not a design flaw.
verdicts.better_fix:
The direction is right, but one part needs fixing. "V-REPLAY covers shadow-logged verdicts" brings back the unjournaled shadow records that :792 (J1-7/J2-9) removed on purpose, and nothing in the paper defines what such a log would be. Instead, use the paper's existing split-mile notation:
- V-REBUILD mile column becomes "3 (eval set) / 4 (all leaves)".
- V-REPLAY mile column becomes "3 (verdicts from the mile-3 shadow tuning runs, recorded as a pre-format-7 test fixture under `oracle/`, not as substrate state) / 4 (every journaled `govern{propose}`)". Add a sentence saying the mile-3 record is temporary scaffolding and does not satisfy J1-7.
- Make the same change to V-SHADOW (:506): "3 (no promote is called by the shadow run) / 4 (no generation leaves Proposed, checked from the journal)".
- Edit mile 3's done-means (:654) so it reads "V-REBUILD (eval set) ... V-REPLAY (fixture arm)".
This doesn't touch any ruled item (R4 shadow-through-mile-4 stays literal), so it needs no owner ruling.

verdicts.reason:
The finding holds. Mile 3 requires V-REBUILD and V-REPLAY to be green "on a real store" (BLUEPRINT_v7.md:654). V-REPLAY's pass condition is "reproduces every journaled `propose` verdict" (:516), and V-REBUILD's is "the eval set and every leaf rebuild byte-identically" (:496). Neither can be met as written at mile 3, for three reasons.

1. **No journaled propose exists before mile 4.** `govern{why: propose}` is a v7 addition, since v6's govern has no propose (:114, row 7). It lives in the format-7 journal (:119, :192, :375), and format 7 and the G1 chain are built at mile 4 (:655). At mile 3 the store is still v5 (landed at mile 0, :643) or v6, so "every journaled propose" is an empty set and the check is vacuous.

2. **The checkpoint leaves depend on mile-4 pieces.** "Every leaf" covers the G3 list at :260-268: fold checkpoints, vector index, recall anchors, USD policy layers, cortex projection, snapshot.json, eval set and verdict.
